# Start here {.unnumbered}

## Before each session

Each session has an overview page with a checklist. Plan about 1.5 to 2 hours.

1. **Read the chapters** of the session in this book and watch the videos inside them. The chapters are complete on their own; the videos walk you through the same ideas.
2. **Try the practice questions** at the end of the session. Solutions are hidden under each question, so try first and then check.
3. **Take the entry quiz on Moodle.** You can try it as often as you like before the deadline; your best attempt counts. Pass at least 3 of the 4 quizzes to earn your cheat sheet for the exam.

Could not prepare? Come anyway and tell the instructor. Each session has a **catch-up sheet** in this book (the last chapter of every session) that gets you ready for the second half of class.

## Spreadsheets, R and Python

You will see three kinds of tool snippets. You do not need to run any of them, but you can copy them with the button in the top-right corner.

**Spreadsheets** are drawn as a grid with column letters and row numbers, so you can see which cells a formula refers to. Green cells contain a formula; the small grey number underneath is the result the formula shows.

```{.sheet title="Example: a formula in D2 multiplies the cells B2 and C2"}
Item | Quantity | Unit price | Total
Inner tube | 4 | 6.50 | =B2*C2 -> 26.00
```

Any spreadsheet program works: Excel, LibreOffice Calc or Google Sheets. Where a function has a different name in different programs, the [spreadsheet functions](appendices/spreadsheet-functions.qmd) appendix gives both.

**R** and **Python** snippets have a coloured label and frame, so you can always tell them apart:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R
```r
4 * 6.50   # 26
```
## Python
```python
4 * 6.50   # 26.0
```
:::

When a snippet shows both languages, pick a tab. The book remembers your choice.

## Your group and your business

You work in a fixed group of 4 to 5 students for all four sessions. Your group runs a small business of its own choosing, in a home market you choose, ideally a country someone in your group knows. That country gives you the currency, the VAT rate and the interest rates you will use.

Throughout the book, the worked examples follow one example business, **Loop Cycles**, a start-up in Gießen (Germany) that refurbishes used bicycles and offers repairs. Your group does the same steps for its own business.
